title: Quotations for Chapter 23 (the gold standard, runs and the lender of last resort): Hansard on Black Friday, 11 May 1866, and on 17 May; the Bank Charter Act 1844; Bagehot's Lombard Street (1873); Andréadès on the crises of 1847, 1857 and 1866; Bordo, Dutton (with Moggridge's comment), McGouldrick and Dornbusch-Frenkel in Bordo and Schwartz (eds.), A Retrospective on the Classical Gold Standard (1984); the Reichsbank, 1876-1900, and Sprague's History of Crises (National Monetary Commission, 1910); the Federal Reserve Act (1913) and the Gold Standard Act (1900); Bryan's First Battle (1896); Keynes (1925, in Essays in Persuasion), Menger (1892), Knapp (1924), Fisher (1896), Rockoff (2009) and Tacitus (Gordon's translation)

notes: Dates and figures that the sources give differently. Bank Rate in 1866: Andréadès (p. 360, rows an_10pct, an_aug6) says 10 per cent from 11 May to 6 August; the Bank of England's table D1 (snapshot boe_millennium_bank_rate_1844_1914) gives 9 per cent on 11 May, 10 per cent from 12 May and 8 per cent from 16 August; the chapter follows D1 and records the difference in its notes on sources. The advances on Government securities on Black Friday: £919,000 in Hansard (row hm_govsec), £929,000 in Andréadès (row an_929); the chapter follows Hansard. The reserve on the morning of 11 May: 'a sum approaching £6,000,000' (Gladstone, row hs_reserve), £5,727,000 (the Governor's letter, in Andréadès, row an_5727), £5,812,000 'just before' (Bagehot, row bg_13m; the weekly return of 9 May in the Bank of England's sheet W2 gives 5.811745 £ m). Bagehot's loans on 'private securities' (rows bg_loans1847, bg_loans1857, bg_loans1866) are the column 'Discounts, advances and other securities' of sheet W2 (16 and 30 October 1847, 24 October and 25 November 1857, 25 April and 30 May 1866); checks/check_ch23.py compares them. Bagehot's reserve of 1,176,000 L. in October 1847 (ch. VII, row bg_reserve1847) is the notes held by the Banking Department on 30 October 1847 in sheet W1 (1.17674 £ m), without its coin; Andréadès (p. 336) puts the same figure on 23 October. The phrase 'rules of the game': Moggridge (row mo_kindersley) dates its first use to Kindersley's evidence to the Macmillan Committee in February 1930; the chapter does not attribute it to Keynes (1925). Bloomfield's counts (rows du_34_60, du_boe) are taken from Dutton's summary; Bloomfield (1959) itself could not be downloaded (FRASER was not reachable from the shell, and the archive.org copy is restricted), so they rest on that one witness; Bordo (rows bo_opposite, bo_managed) quotes Bloomfield's conclusions. Bryan's vote counts (rows br_votes, br_plurality, br_19436) are his own figures in his own book. The OCR texts are quoted as they read; the notes give the readings where they differ.
